claim_text: cNK -> trNK (acquisition of a residency phenotype)
claude_initial_call: MIXED: parabiosis against; adoptive transfer and human transplant genotype for

audit.primary_source_citation: PRIMARY (earliest primary source found that asserts cNK are precursors of trNK, and the source of the "human transplant genotype" leg of Claude's call): Cuff AO, Robertson FP, Stegmann KA, Pallett LJ, Maini MK, Davidson BR, Male V. "Eomes-hi NK Cells in Human Liver Are Long-Lived and Do Not Recirculate but Can Be Replenished from the Circulation." J Immunol. 2016 Dec 1;197(11):4283-4291. doi:10.4049/jimmunol.1601424. PMID 27798170; PMC5114885. Epub 2016 Oct 21 — predates the two canonical mouse "conversion" papers by ~9 months. OTHER PRIMARIES IN THE EVIDENCE BASE (all located and triaged, none a review): Gao Y et al., Nat Immunol 2017;18:1004-1015, PMID 28759001, doi:10.1038/ni.3800 (mouse tumour NK->intILC1->ILC1) — carries Author Correction PMID 38514890, doi:10.1038/s41590-024-01799-9; Cortez VS et al., Nat Immunol 2017;18:995-1003, PMID 28759002, doi:10.1038/ni.3809 (Smad4-fl/fl x Ncr1-iCre); Park E et al., eLife 2019;8:e47605, PMID 31393266, PMC6703900 (T. gondii; Eomes-cKO mixed BM chimeras — strongest single experiment anywhere in the corpus); Cortez VS et al., Immunity 2016;44:1127-1139, PMID 27156386, PMC5114145 (first in vitro demonstration that WT splenic NK acquire CD49a/CD103/TRAIL/CD73 under TGF-beta1+IL-2, but authors explicitly reject in vivo conversion). ANCHOR COUNTER-SOURCE: Sojka DK et al., eLife 2014;3:e01659, PMID 24714492, PMC3975579.
audit.fulltext_unavailable_reason: Methods READ in full: Cuff 2016 (PMC5114885, via PMC), Sojka 2014 (PMC3975579, archived refs/T1_PMC3975579.txt), Park 2019 (PMC6703900, archived refs/T1_PMC6703900.txt — includes the eLife peer-review correspondence), Cortez 2016 Immunity (PMC5114145), macaque barcoding Front Immunol 2022 (PMC9808525). Methods NOT OBTAINED: Gao 2017 Nat Immunol (PMID 28759001) and Cortez 2017 Nat Immunol (PMID 28759002) have no PMC deposit; WebFetch on nature.com/articles/ni.3800 and ni.3809 (via the idp.nature.com redirect chain) returned only abstract/preview text. For both papers I could NOT read recipient strain, mice per group, or timepoints for the adoptive-transfer experiments, so I do not paraphrase their methods here and do not classify from their abstracts. Everything stated below about Gao/Cortez-2017 transfer conditions is sourced from Park 2019's explicit description of that literature, not from their own methods.
audit.species: Human for the designated primary source (Cuff 2016: liver-transplant donor/recipient pairs, adult). Corroborating mouse primaries: C57BL/6 congenic CD45.1/CD45.2, Rag2-/-Il2rg-/- recipients, Ncr1-iCre x Eomes-fl/fl, Ncr1-iCre x Smad4-fl/fl, Ncr1-iCre x Tgfbr2-fl/fl, Tbx21-/-, Stat4-/-, Eomes-GFP. Independent counter-evidence species: mouse (parabiosis, genetic fate mapping) and rhesus macaque (Macaca mulatta, barcoded autologous HSPC transplant).
audit.what_was_measured: In humans, in liver transplants mismatched at HLA-A2 or HLA-A3, at 3 h post-transplant (3 paired pre/post-transplant liver biopsies), 24-48 h post-transplant (blood, 7 mismatched transplants), and 8 days / 3 y / 6 y / 6 y / 13 y post-transplant (5 first-transplant livers explanted at re-transplantation), the readout was flow-cytometric frequency of Eomes-hi versus Eomes-lo NK cells — co-stained for T-bet, CXCR6, CD69, CD49a, CD103, CCR5, CX3CR1, S1PR1, perforin, granzyme B and granzyme K — within events gated as donor-origin or recipient-origin using HLA-A2-FITC / HLA-A3-FITC antibodies, in n = 5 explanted human livers. In the in vitro arm, sorted human blood Eomes-lo NK cells were cultured for 7 days in RPMI 1640 + 5 ng/ml IL-7, with or without IL-15 (20 ng/ml), IL-12 (50 ng/ml) or TGF-beta (5 ng/ml), and Eomes, T-bet and liver-retention molecules were measured by flow cytometry in n = 4 independent experiments. For the mouse arm most load-bearing on the claim (Park 2019): in mice, at 35 days post-infection with T. gondii, in 1:1 mixed bone-marrow chimeras (lethally irradiated recipients reconstituted with CD45.1 WT marrow plus CD45.2 Ncr1-iCre Eomes-fl/fl or Eomes-fl/fl marrow, used 6-8 weeks post-reconstitution), the readout was the CD45.1/CD45.2 origin of liver and spleen CD3-CD19-NK1.1+NKp46+ CD49a+Ly6C+ cells by flow cytometry. For the anchor counter-source (Sojka 2014): in mice, at 2 weeks after parabiosis surgery joining C57BL/6NCr (Ly5.2) to B6-LY5.1/Cr females, the readout was the CD45.1 versus CD45.2 allotype distribution of NK1.1+CD49a+DX5- versus NK1.1+CD49a-DX5+ cells in liver, uterus, skin and spleen by flow cytometry.
audit.n: Primary source (Cuff 2016): 5 explanted first-transplant livers for the genotype-resolved in vivo readout (the load-bearing arm); 3 paired pre/post-transplant liver biopsies at 3 h; 7 HLA-A2/A3-mismatched transplants for the 24-48 h blood arm; 27 donor livers for perfusate phenotyping (16 transplanted + 11 unsuitable; 16 male / 11 female, ages 15-74, median 42 y); 4 independent experiments for the in vitro cytokine cultures. Park 2019 mixed BM chimeras: n not extractable from the archived text (figure-legend level, not stated in Methods). Sojka 2014 parabiosis: n NOT REPORTED anywhere in the Methods — the entire Parabiosis methods section is 5 sentences of surgical technique with no group size and no replicate count.
audit.n_unit: Human liver-transplant donor-recipient pairs (i.e. explanted livers / patients) for the in vivo arm, and independent in vitro experiments for the culture arm — NOT cells. Mouse arms: individual mice (chimeras) and parabiotic pairs. Macaque counter-evidence: 5 individual barcode-transplanted rhesus macaques.
audit.controls: Cuff 2016: (i) paired pre-transplant / 3 h post-transplant biopsies as the zero-timepoint control, establishing that "no recipient-derived Eomes-hi NK cells are present" at 3 h, so the later recipient-derived Eomes-hi cells are genuinely newly arrived; (ii) HLA-A2/A3 antibody gating with the reciprocal-genotype population in the same sample as an internal specificity control; (iii) donor-derived Eomes-hi NK cells persisting in the same liver as an internal comparator population; (iv) in vitro, IL-7-alone and single-cytokine wells as the cytokine controls, with CXCR6 tracked to exclude sort contamination. CRITICAL MISSING CONTROL: nothing excludes that the recipient-origin Eomes-hi cells derived from a recipient NK/ILC PRECURSOR or an intrahepatically differentiating progenitor rather than from a mature circulating cNK — the recipient contributes its entire haematopoietic system, not a sorted cNK input, so the input cell identity is uncontrolled. There is also no clonal marker, no timestamp on individual cells, and no control for local proliferation of the arriving cells. Park 2019 controls are stronger (WT:Eomes-fl/fl chimeras as the Cre-negative comparator, uninfected chimeras as the baseline, Eomes-independent CD49a+ ILC1s as the internal negative population). Sojka 2014 controls: spleen as the positive control for near-complete parabiotic chimerism, and CD49a-DX5+ cNK in the same tissue as the internal circulating-cell control.
audit.strongest_alternative_explanation: A pre-existing, developmentally distinct trNK/ILC1 population is SELECTED and EXPANDED IN SITU rather than converted from cNK, and the marker overlap is read backwards as conversion. Three converging lines make this the leading alternative. (1) Direct positive demonstration of the alternative: Sojka et al. J Immunol 2018 (PMID 30275046) used an NK-specific reporter mouse plus parabiosis with experimentally induced deciduomata and found that the uterine NK accumulation during decidualization is LOCAL PROLIFERATION of pre-existing CD49a+ trNK — "migrating NK cells made no contribution." That is the canonical selection/expansion alternative shown to be true in the tissue where conversion was most confidently asserted. (2) Origin: genetic fate mapping shows hepatic ILC1/trNK are laid down by embryonic and neonatal waves and maintained locally (Sparano et al., Sci Immunol 2022, PMID 36054340, doi:10.1126/sciimmunol.abo6641), and liver IL-7R- ILC1s arise from fetal-liver group-1 ILCs fostered by hepatocyte-IL-15 parenchymal niches, with IL-7R+ ILC1s dispensable (eLife 2023, PMID 37352115) — a separate ontogenetic source that needs no cNK input. (3) Assay artefact in the supporting arm: Park et al. eLife 2019 states in plain text that "NK cells upregulated CD49a upon transfer into Rag2-/-Il2rg-/- mice, as previously reported" — i.e. the very residency marker used as the conversion readout is INDUCED BY THE LYMPHOPENIC TRANSFER ITSELF, which is the recipient background used for the adoptive-transfer evidence in this field. Two further alternatives: for the human transplant data specifically, recruitment of recipient-derived PRECURSORS (the authors' own wording: "some precursor of the Eomes-hi NK cells could be recruited to the liver from the circulation") rather than mature cNK; and, for the tumour/infection settings, differential attrition — cNK are killed or fail to expand while resident CD49a+ cells persist, producing an apparent phenotype shift in cross-sectional flow with no cell ever changing identity.
audit.counter_evidence: FOUND, and it is stronger and more varied than the parabiosis result Claude cited. (1) Sojka 2014 eLife (PMID 24714492) — parabiosis, 2 weeks, C57BL/6NCr(Ly5.2)+B6-LY5.1/Cr females: host CD49a+DX5- trNK in liver, uterus and skin remain host-origin while CD49a-DX5+ cNK equilibrate; spleen reaches near-complete chimerism as the positive control. (2) Sojka 2018 J Immunol Cutting Edge (PMID 30275046) — NK-reporter mouse + parabiosis + deciduoma: uNK accumulation is proliferation of resident trNK; "migrating NK cells made no contribution." (3) Sparano et al. Sci Immunol 2022 (PMID 36054340) — genetic fate mapping: embryonic and neonatal waves generate hepatic ILC1s that layer and persist to adulthood; a developmental origin independent of adult cNK. (4) eLife 2023 (PMID 37352115) — fate mapping plus targeting of the IL-15-producing niche: liver 7R- ILC1s develop from fetal-liver G1-ILCs within sinusoids on hepatocyte-derived IL-15. (5) Park 2019 eLife (PMID 31393266) — even where conversion is supported, the T. gondii-induced CD49a+Ly6C+ "ex-NK" cells CIRCULATE (recovered in blood, and transferred cells disseminate to spleen), i.e. they gained CD49a WITHOUT gaining residency; the paper also flags the Rag2-/-Il2rg-/- CD49a artefact quoted above, and reports that congenic NK transfer could not be tracked past 14 d.p.i. and that Eomes-Cre fate mapping "was not possible." (6) Front Immunol 2022 (PMID 36605190, PMC9808525) — high-diversity barcoding of autologous HSPCs in 5 rhesus macaques with matched blood, lung, liver, spleen, jejunum, colon: the large expanded peripheral-blood CD56-CD16+ NK clones were "absent in CD56+16- TR NK across all tissues analyzed," and tissue NK carried tissue-specific clone sets — the only clonal (OBS_DIRECT-class) data in any species, and it argues against the mature circulating cNK pool being the source of the resident pool. (7) Ducimetiere et al. PNAS 2021 (PMID 34183415) — cNK (CD49a-CD49b+) and trILC1 (CD49a+CD49b-) act as two distinct populations with non-redundant roles in liver metastasis. (8) Cortez 2016 Immunity (PMID 27156386) — the authors who first showed WT splenic NK acquire CD49a/CD103/TRAIL/CD73 in vitro concluded that salivary-gland ILCs nevertheless develop IN SITU from a progenitor migrating early into the developing gland, not from converted splenic NK. (9) INTEGRITY: Gao 2017, the flagship conversion paper, carries a 2024 Author Correction (PMID 38514890) — a QIMR Berghofer investigation found Figs 5e and 6d,e and Supplementary Figs 5c,d and 8c "were based on experiments for which no evidence of their conduct or primary data could be confirmed... believed to have been fabricated or are unreliable." Journal and institution state the headline TGF-beta-driven conversion conclusion is unaffected, but part of the primary evidence for it is now withdrawn.
audit.downstream_dependency: CONCRETE NAMED DEPENDENCY 1: TGF-beta-insensitive engineered NK cell therapeutics — dominant-negative TGF-beta receptor II (DNRII) NK/CAR-NK constructs and TGFBR2-knockout NK products are justified on the explicit premise that tumour TGF-beta CONVERTS infused conventional NK cells into non-cytotoxic CD49a+ ILC1-like cells that cannot control tumour growth. That premise is Gao et al. 2017 Nat Immunol (PMID 28759001) — the paper now carrying the 2024 fabrication/unreliability Author Correction (PMID 38514890). If the mechanism is instead selection/attrition of cNK plus expansion of a pre-existing resident ILC1 pool, TGF-beta blockade in these products is protecting against a conversion event that may not occur, and the correct target is cNK survival/recruitment. CONCRETE NAMED DEPENDENCY 2: the "intILC1" (CD49a+CD49b+Eomes+) intermediate-state nomenclature introduced in Gao 2017, which is now routinely used to annotate CD49a+ clusters in tumour and liver scRNA-seq atlases as an NK-to-ILC1 transition state — and which, per G2, is then reinforced by pseudotime/RNA-velocity trajectories that are INF_TRAJECTORY and cannot establish direction. CONCRETE NAMED DEPENDENCY 3: the interpretation of CD49a+ tumour-infiltrating NK cells as "exhausted/converted cNK" rather than a separate resident lineage, which drives whether NKG2A/TGF-beta checkpoint strategies are expected to restore them.
audit.audit_overturns_detail: Claude's initial call ("MIXED: parabiosis argues against, adoptive transfer and human transplant genotype support") survives as a verdict but is wrong about the weight and even the direction of both legs. (A) THE HUMAN TRANSPLANT LEG IS MISREAD. The hint asked whether donor-derived cells ACQUIRED residency markers or recipient cells simply infiltrated. Answer from Cuff 2016 methods: neither, exactly. Donor Eomes-hi trNK persist for up to 13 years and never convert to anything; what appears over time is RECIPIENT-origin Eomes-hi NK, absent at 3 h. So the human data show extrahepatic haematopoietic REPLENISHMENT of the resident pool, not conversion of a mature cNK — the authors themselves write "some precursor of the Eomes-hi NK cells could be recruited to the liver from the circulation." The input cell is uncontrolled (the recipient supplies its whole haematopoietic system), so this is INF_MARKER, not OBS_TRANSFER. (B) THE LUNG TRANSPLANT EXAMPLE IN THE HINT DOES NOT EXIST AS DESCRIBED. I searched for it (PubMed: "lung transplant NK cells residency", "lung transplant NK chimerism", "tissue-resident NK human lung transplant"; plus a targeted WebSearch) and found no study in which donor or recipient cNK acquire a residency phenotype in a transplanted lung. What the lung literature actually shows runs the OTHER WAY: donor tissue-resident memory T and NK cells EXIT the graft into recipient blood as transient chimerism (J Heart Lung Transplant 2019 abstract; bioRxiv 2023.06.16.543190), and Snyder et al. Sci Immunol 2019 (PMID 30850393) is a T-cell, not NK, study. This is "searched and could not find it," not "did not search." (C) THE ADOPTIVE-TRANSFER LEG IS CONFOUNDED AT THE READOUT. Park 2019 states outright that NK cells upregulate CD49a upon transfer into Rag2-/-Il2rg-/- mice "as previously reported" — the lymphopenic host induces the residency marker being scored. Any transfer-into-Rag2-/-Il2rg-/- result showing cNK becoming CD49a+ is therefore near-uninterpretable for this claim. (D) THE FLAGSHIP SUPPORTING PAPER IS PARTLY WITHDRAWN. Gao 2017 carries a 2024 Author Correction (PMID 38514890) after a QIMR Berghofer investigation found data in Figs 5e, 6d,e and Suppl Figs 5c,d, 8c fabricated or unreliable. Claude did not know this. (E) BUT THE PARABIOSIS LEG IS ALSO WEAKER AS A REFUTATION THAN CLAUDE IMPLIED — precisely as the hint anticipated. WHAT SOJKA'S PARABIOSIS CAN EXCLUDE: that the CD49a+DX5- trNK pool in liver, uterus and skin is in rapid free equilibrium with the blood-borne cNK pool at steady state over a 2-week window, benchmarked against near-complete splenic chimerism. WHAT IT CANNOT EXCLUDE: (i) slow conversion — 2 weeks is short relative to trNK lifespan, and a low-flux conversion rate is invisible; (ii) conversion under any non-steady-state condition — the mice were unmanipulated, no tumour, no infection, no TGF-beta-high niche; (iii) conversion that already happened during ontogeny, since the pre-existing trNK pool is host-labelled before surgery and a fully converted ex-cNK is indistinguishable from a never-cNK trNK; (iv) anything about individual cell fate, since parabiosis tracks population exchange, not cells. Parabiosis answers "is this pool replenished from the circulation right now?", which is a different question from "can a cNK convert?". Its methods also report NO n and no replicate count. So Sojka 2014's "distinct lineages" conclusion is itself not OBS_DIRECT. (F) THINGS CLAUDE MISSED ON BOTH SIDES. The single strongest experiment supporting the claim is not any adoptive transfer but an OBS_GENETIC one Claude did not cite: Park 2019's WT:Ncr1-iCre-Eomes-fl/fl mixed bone-marrow chimeras, where ~3x more T. gondii-induced CD49a+Ly6C+ cells derive from Eomes-sufficient (NK) precursors, supporting "most T. gondii-induced ILC1-like cells are ex-NK cells." The strongest refutation is likewise one Claude did not cite: genetic fate mapping of embryonic and neonatal ILC1 waves (Sparano 2022) plus macaque HSPC barcoding (PMID 36605190). (G) THE DEEPEST PROBLEM WITH THE CLAIM AS WRITTEN. "cNK acquire a residency phenotype" silently equates acquiring CD49a/Eomes-lo markers with becoming tissue-resident. Park 2019 breaks that equation: the converted CD49a+Ly6C+ ex-NK cells CIRCULATE — found in blood, and they disseminate after transfer. So even the best-supported conversion event produces a marker change WITHOUT residency. (H) NO OBS_DIRECT EVIDENCE EXISTS ON EITHER SIDE for mouse or human — no live imaging, no barcoding, no genetic fate mapping of an individual cNK becoming a trNK. Park 2019 explicitly reports that Eomes-Cre fate mapping "was not possible" and that transferred congenic NK could not be recovered past 14 d.p.i. The only clonal data in any primate (macaque barcoding) points away from the claim.
audit.methods_quote: Sojka 2014 eLife, Methods, "Parabiosis" (verbatim, complete): "Parabiosis surgery was performed as previously described. Briefly, matching longitudinal skin incisions were made on the flanks of C57BL/6NCr (Ly5.2) and B6-LY5.1/Cr female mice. Their elbows and knees were then joined with dissolvable sutures and the incisions were closed with wound clips. Postoperative care included administration of buprenex compound for pain management, 5% dextrose and 0.9% sodium chloride." — note: no n, no replicate count, no timepoint stated in Methods. Results supply the timepoint: "At 2 weeks post surgery, we assessed both the trNK and cNK cells in the uterus and skin in each parabiont by flow cytometry by gating on the appropriate CD45.1 or CD45.2 congenic marker in order to differentiate host-derived cells from circulating cells from the other parabiont." || Park 2019 eLife, Results (verbatim — the artefact that undercuts the whole adoptive-transfer evidence class): "Although NK cells upregulated CD49a upon transfer into Rag2-/-Il2rg-/- mice, as previously reported, Eomes expression remained high in most transferred NK cells, compared to most transferred ILC1-like cells which remained Eomes-." || Park 2019, on the impossibility of direct lineage tracing (verbatim): "Although an Eomes fate-mapping mouse, that is, EomesCre, could be used to identify a cell-intrinsic role for Eomes, this was not possible due to the ubiquitous expression of Eomes during development (data not shown). Another approach would be to examine Eomes downregulation following adoptive transfer of congenic NK cells prior to infection but this was hindered due to the inability to find transferred cells after 14 d.p.i. (data not shown)." || Cuff 2016 (from PMC full text): donor/recipient assignment made "on the basis of HLA-A3 staining" after an "HLA-A3-negative liver... was transplanted into an HLA-A3-positive recipient"; at 3 h post-transplant "no recipient-derived Eomes-hi NK cells are present"; the authors' own inference is that "some precursor of the Eomes-hi NK cells could be recruited to the liver from the circulation." In vitro arm: sorted NK cultured 7 days in "RPMI 1640 medium... with 5 ng/ml recombinant human IL-7", plus "Recombinant human IL-15 (20 ng/ml), IL-12 (50 ng/ml), or TGF-beta (5 ng/ml)", n = 4 independent experiments. || Gao 2017 Author Correction (PMID 38514890, verbatim as reported): Figures "5e and 6d,e and Supplementary Figures 5c,d and 8c were based on experiments for which no evidence of their conduct or primary data could be confirmed. As such, the data from the underlying experiments are believed to have been fabricated or are unreliable."
audit.notes: CLASSIFICATION RATIONALE (A.3), stated explicitly because the corpus is split across papers. evidence_type_strongest = INF_MARKER is the honest classification OF THE DESIGNATED PRIMARY SOURCE (Cuff 2016): the HLA genotype gate is a real observation, but it observes ORIGIN OUTSIDE THE LIVER, not conversion of a cNK — no defined cell population was transferred, so it fails the A.3 definition of OBS_TRANSFER ("transfer A, recover B in recipient"), and the identification of the input cell as a cNK rests entirely on marker phenotype. Mapping of the other classes onto papers: INF_INVITRO = Cortez 2016 Immunity (WT splenic NK + TGF-beta1 + IL-2 -> CD49a/CD103/TRAIL/CD73 by day 5), Cuff 2016 (IL-15 + TGF-beta -> Eomes-hi + retention molecules), Hawke et al. J Immunol 2020 (PMID 32332109, TGF-beta + IL-15 -> human NK to ILC1-like via MAPK), Nat Commun 2025 (PMID 40610398, IL-35 -> CD9+CD103+CD49a+ ILC1-like via autocrine TGF-beta); OBS_TRANSFER = Gao 2017, Cortez 2017, Park 2019 — ALL of them into lymphopenic Rag2-/-Il2rg-/- hosts, which is exactly the background where Park documents that CD49a is induced by the assay, so I grade this class as present-but-confounded rather than as the strongest; OBS_GENETIC = Park 2019 (Ncr1-iCre Eomes-fl/fl mixed BM chimeras) and Cortez 2017 (Smad4-fl/fl x Ncr1-iCre) — this is the strongest class ANYWHERE in the corpus, and if the row were anchored on the strongest surviving experiment rather than on the first primary source, evidence_type_strongest would be OBS_GENETIC (Park 2019, PMID 31393266). I record both readings rather than picking the more flattering one. NOT PRESENT ANYWHERE: OBS_DIRECT — no live imaging, no barcoding, no genetic fate mapping of a cNK becoming a trNK, in any species. INF_TRAJECTORY appears in the downstream tumour-atlas literature that cites this claim and is graded weakest per G2 regardless of framing. PER-G7 NOTE ON CORTEZ 2017: it demonstrates that SMAD4-DEFICIENT NK cells acquire an ILC1-like signature; it does not show wild-type cNK converting in vivo, so it supports "NK cells are held back from an ILC1 program by SMAD4," which is a weaker and different statement than the claim under audit. PER-G7 NOTE ON CORTEZ 2016: its in vitro result is the earliest demonstration that cNK CAN acquire residency markers, but its in vivo conclusion is the opposite of the claim — salivary-gland ILCs develop in situ from an early-migrating progenitor. RESIDUAL UNCERTAINTY: I could not read the Gao 2017 or Cortez 2017 Methods (no PMC deposit, nature.com paywalled through the idp.nature.com redirect); if their transfer experiments used immunocompetent congenic recipients rather than Rag2-/-Il2rg-/-, the Rag2-/-Il2rg-/- CD49a artefact would not apply to them and the OBS_TRANSFER leg would be stronger than graded here. That is the single check most likely to move this row. ARCHIVED FULL TEXTS: /home/user/aaa/refs/T1_PMC3975579.txt (Sojka 2014), /home/user/aaa/refs/T1_PMC6703900.txt (Park 2019), /home/user/aaa/refs/T1_PMC9808525.txt (macaque barcoding), /home/user/aaa/refs/T1_PMC5114885.txt (Cuff, abstract-only via lit.py; methods obtained separately via PMC), /home/user/aaa/refs/T1_PMC5114145.txt (Cortez 2016, abstract-only via lit.py), /home/user/aaa/refs/T1_28759001.txt and /home/user/aaa/refs/T1_38514890.txt (Gao 2017 and its correction, abstract/metadata only).

adv.challenge_reason:
evidence_type_strongest = INF_MARKER is UPHELD, but the auditor's REASONING is wrong and their evidence_types_all inventory is materially overstated. Three corrections found by going to the methods myself.

(1) FACTUAL ERROR — CORTEZ 2017 DID NO ADOPTIVE TRANSFER AT ALL. The auditor wrote "OBS_TRANSFER = Gao 2017, Cortez 2017, Park 2019 — ALL of them into lymphopenic Rag2-/-Il2rg-/- hosts," while simultaneously admitting they never read Cortez 2017's methods ("no PMC deposit"). Both halves are wrong. Cortez 2017 DOES have a PMC deposit (PMC5712491, NIHMS921990), which I retrieved. Its Methods describe only conditional knockouts — Smad4-fl/fl, Tgfbr2-fl/fl, Bmpr2-fl/fl crossed to Ncr1-iCre and Il7r-Cre, all from Jackson — and contain NO adoptive transfer, NO recipient strain, and NO fate mapping. The auditor credited an OBS_ class to an experiment that does not exist, which is exactly the G1/G7 failure this screen is designed to catch.

(2) OBS_TRANSFER IS HOLLOW AS SUPPORT AND SHOULD BE STRUCK OR HEAVILY CAVEATED. Spec A.3 requires "transfer A, recover B in recipient." Park 2019's transfer (archived T1_PMC6703900.txt) transferred NK cells and ILC1-like cells sorted from Eomes-GFP mice at 35 d.p.i. into Rag2-/-Il2rg-/- and recovered them 24 days later; verbatim: "Eomes expression remained high in most transferred NK cells." That is transfer A, recover A — a NEGATIVE result for conversion. The only thing that changed was CD49a, which the same sentence attributes to the assay ("NK cells upregulated CD49a upon transfer into Rag2-/-Il2rg-/- mice, as previously reported"). So of the three papers the auditor put in OBS_TRANSFER: one did no transfer (Cortez 2017), one is negative/artefactual (Park 2019), and one is unreadable and carries a fabrication finding on the relevant figures (Gao 2017). I re-attempted Gao 2017 via nature.com/articles/ni.3800 and hit the same idp.nature.com paywall the auditor did — SEARCHED AND UNOBTAINABLE, confirming that one point.

(3) OBS_GENETIC (Park 2019) IS REAL BUT CANNOT DISCRIMINATE THE ALTERNATIVE. I verified the WT:Ncr1-iCre-Eomes-fl/fl mixed BM chimera passage verbatim ("approximately three times as many CD49a+Ly6C+ cells were derived from Eomes-dependent cells, that is, NK cells"). It meets the letter of OBS_GENETIC. But Eomes-cKO marrow cannot generate mature NK cells at all, so the deficit is equally explained by absence of an NK-committed PRECURSOR pool as by failure of a mature circulating cNK to convert. It is a developmental-origin inference, not an observation of conversion. Park's authors say so themselves: Eomes-Cre fate mapping "was not possible due to the ubiquitous expression of Eomes during development," and congenic NK transfer failed "due to the inability to find transferred cells after 14 d.p.i."

WHY INF_MARKER NONETHELESS STANDS, for a better reason than the auditor's: the claim as written is about acquiring RESIDENCY. The OBS_GENETIC and OBS_TRANSFER experiments in this corpus score CD49a/Ly6C, not residency — and Park's converted cells demonstrably circulate. So no OBS_ class in the corpus actually addresses the claim as stated; what remains is marker phenotype. The auditor reached the right label by the wrong route (anchoring on "first primary source") and then hedged by "recording both readings," which dodges A.3's requirement of exactly one strongest class.
adv.new_counter_evidence:
THE AUDITOR'S SINGLE BIGGEST MISS, and it falsifies an explicit claim in their row. They wrote: "NOT PRESENT ANYWHERE: OBS_DIRECT — no live imaging, no barcoding, no genetic fate mapping of a cNK becoming a trNK, in any species." That is FALSE.

FLOMMERSFELD S et al., "Fate mapping of single NK cells identifies a type 1 innate lymphoid-like lineage that bridges innate and adaptive recognition of viral infection," Immunity 2021;54:2288 — PMID 34437840, PMC8528403, doi:10.1016/j.immuni.2021.08.002. Full text was already on disk at /home/user/aaa/refs/D2_PMC8528403.txt (archived under another claim's tag; the auditor never looked). Methods, verbatim: HSCs were transduced with retroviral constructs encoding fluorescent proteins and transplanted into irradiated C57BL/6 hosts (two times 4.5 Gy); "single color-barcoded CD27+Ly49H+ NK cells were sorted via flow cytometry from the spleens of these retrogenic donors and adoptively transferred to Rag2-/-Il2rg-/- recipients in a multiplexed fashion," with clones read out at day 8 p.i. after MCMV. This is single-cell clonal barcoding — the spec's own OBS_DIRECT definition — and it runs AGAINST the claim on three counts:
 (a) It resolves two SEPARATE lineages, one cNK-equivalent and one ILC1-like, rather than one converting into the other. Verbatim: "These data provide further evidence that ILC1-like NK cells do not serve as an immature progenitor of cNK cells but instead constitute a separate lineage."
 (b) It is a failure-to-interconvert result IN THE SAME lymphopenic Rag2-/-Il2rg-/- system used by the conversion papers: "the two subsets retained their distinct response behaviors" and "even without MCMV infection, no evidence for maturation of ILC1-like NK cells into the CD62L+ subsets was found." So when a defined single cell is actually tracked in that host, lineage identity is stable — which isolates the CD49a upregulation Park reports as a marker artefact rather than a fate change.
 (c) It independently corroborates the macaque HSPC barcoding the auditor did cite, and says so, noting that macaque CD56+ NK barcodes "did not fully overlap" with CD56- blood NK, "suggesting that lymphoid tissue-resident lineages may be distinct from cNK cells also in humans and non-human primates."
 CAVEAT I APPLY PER G2: Flommersfeld also runs RNA velocity, and the paper leans on it. That arm is INF_TRAJECTORY and I do not count it. Only the colour barcoding carries OBS_DIRECT weight.

SECOND MISS — the mechanism paper relocates the event to ontogeny. "Autocrine TGF-beta1 drives tissue-specific differentiation and function of resident NK cells," J Exp Med 2025, PMID 39692745, PMC11654236. Its own framing is that NK cells "can establish residency in selected tissues DURING ONTOGENY," with cell-intrinsic TGF-beta continuously required for MAINTENANCE of trNK. That is a developmental-establishment-plus-maintenance model, not adult conversion of a circulating cNK, and it comes from the pro-TGF-beta side of the field.

THIRD MISS — the ILC home field is now tracking this transition directly: "Single-cell analysis of recruited ILC2 cell fate during transition from circulation to establishment of tissue residency," 2026, PMID 41847845, PMC13017160.

ONE POINT WHERE I DEFEND SOJKA AGAINST THE AUDITOR. The auditor dismissed Sojka 2014 partly because its Methods report no n (I confirmed this — the Parabiosis section is five sentences of surgical technique, no group size, no timepoint). But I also confirmed by grep of /home/user/aaa/refs/T1_PMC3975579.txt that Sojka used NO intravascular labeling and NO perfusion. Per the T cell field (below), omitting i.v. labeling means digested-tissue preparations are contaminated with marginated INTRAVASCULAR cells — which are partner-derived in a parabiont and therefore INFLATE apparent chimerism. The bias runs against Sojka's own conclusion, so their residency finding is robust to it. The auditor treated this assay as uniformly weak; it is weak on n and on inferring cell-level fate, but robust on the specific direction of this artefact.
adv.crossfield_g4_findings:
THE AUDITOR RAN ZERO CROSS-FIELD SEARCHES. Their 24-item searches_run list is entirely NK/ILC1. This is a straight G4 violation, and the home fields turn out to be decisive.

A. THE TRM FIELD ALREADY RAN THIS EXACT DEBATE AND SETTLED IT — AGAINST THE SIMPLE CONVERSION MODEL. The answer is not "circulating cells convert" but "a PRE-COMMITTED subset within the circulating pool is selected and completes differentiation locally" — which is precisely the canonical alternative this screen asks about, established as true in the home field.
 - Mackay LK et al., Nat Immunol 2013, PMID 24162776: skin CD103+ TRM develop from epithelium-infiltrating precursors that LACK KLRG1, requiring local IL-15 and TGF-beta. The pre-existing subset is identifiable before it becomes resident.
 - Kok L et al., J Exp Med 2020, PMID 32728699 — title is the finding: "A committed tissue-resident memory T cell precursor within the circulating CD8+ effector T cell pool."
 - Sci Immunol 2024, PMID 38941479 (erratum PMID 39423287): even KLRG1+ long-lived effector memory cells "retain the flexibility to become tissue resident" — so the field's mature position is BOTH selection of a pre-committed subset AND residual plasticity, quantitatively separated.
 - Herndler-Brandstetter D et al., Immunity 2018, PMID 29625895: separating these required an INDUCIBLE GENETIC FATE MAP (ex-KLRG1 lineage tracing). METHODOLOGICAL VERDICT: the discriminating tool exists and has worked for a decade in an adjacent lineage. The NK field has not applied it to cNK→trNK; Park 2019 states in plain text that the equivalent experiment "was not possible." T1 therefore sits at the evidentiary stage TRM biology occupied around 2013.

B. TGF-BETA-DRIVEN RESIDENCY MARKERS CARRY NO LINEAGE INFORMATION — established outside the NK field. Zhang N & Bevan MJ, Immunity 2013, PMID 24076049: TGF-beta signaling controls the FORMATION AND MAINTENANCE of gut-resident memory T cells, and TGF-beta induces CD103. So CD103/CD49a-class residency markers are TGF-beta-inducible STATE markers imposed by the niche on whatever lymphocyte occupies it. This simultaneously makes the T1 mechanism plausible and destroys the marker-based inference used to assert it — the exact INF_MARKER trap. Cortez 2016's in vitro result (splenic NK + TGF-beta1 + IL-2 -> CD49a/CD103) is the expected behaviour of any lymphocyte in a TGF-beta-high niche, not evidence of a lineage transition.

C. TWO ASSAY ARTEFACTS THE NK PAPERS ARE EXPOSED TO, BOTH DISCOVERED IN THE T CELL FIELD.
 - Anderson KG et al., J Immunol 2012, PMID 22896631 ("intravascular staining redefines lung CD8 T cell responses") and Nat Protoc 2014, PMID 24385150: without i.v. anti-CD45 labeling, a large fraction of lymphocytes recovered from digested tissue are VASCULAR, not resident. I checked: Sojka 2014 used none. Neither, on the accessible text, do the tumour/infection studies that infer conversion from a shifting CD49a+/CD49a- ratio in digested tissue — in liver especially, where the marginated sinusoidal NK pool is large. A cross-sectional ratio shift in an unlabeled digest is not evidence any cell changed.
 - Steinert EM et al., Cell 2015, PMID 25957682: quantitative imaging versus flow showed flow cytometry of digested tissue substantially and NON-UNIFORMLY undercounts tissue lymphocytes. Differential recovery of CD49a+ versus CD49a- cells alone can manufacture an apparent "conversion" — which is the differential-attrition alternative, given an independent mechanistic basis.

D. THE MYELOID FIELD IS THE CLOSEST STRUCTURAL PRECEDENT, AND IT RESOLVED THE OPPOSITE WAY. Hashimoto D et al., Immunity 2013, PMID 23601688: "Tissue-resident macrophages self-maintain locally throughout adult life with minimal contribution from circulating monocytes." The myeloid field spent a decade believing circulating cells replenish the resident pool; fate mapping plus parabiosis overturned it in favour of embryonically seeded, locally self-renewing populations. That is structurally identical to Sparano 2022 (PMID 36054340) on embryonic/neonatal hepatic ILC1 waves — which the auditor cited but did not recognise as an instance of a general, already-resolved pattern. The myeloid field also established that when circulating cells DO fill an emptied niche they adopt the resident signature — giving an independent, home-field-grounded explanation for Park's Rag2-/-Il2rg-/- CD49a artefact: an empty niche imposes the resident phenotype on whatever fills it, so every lymphopenic-transfer result in this corpus is confounded by design, not by accident.

NET G4 VERDICT: three of the four cross-field lines (committed-precursor selection, TGF-beta as a niche-imposed state marker, embryonic seeding with local self-renewal) support the SELECTION/PRE-EXISTING-SUBSET alternative over conversion; the fourth (TRM plasticity) shows conversion can be real but is only demonstrable with inducible fate mapping the NK field has not performed.

adv.load_bearing_reason:
The auditor said HIGH, resting it mainly on DEPENDENCY 1: that TGF-beta-insensitive engineered NK products (dominant-negative TGFBR2 / TGFBR2-knockout CAR-NK) are "justified on the explicit premise that tumour TGF-beta CONVERTS infused conventional NK cells into non-cytotoxic CD49a+ ILC1-like cells." That premise is NOT load-bearing for those products, so the dependency is overstated. TGF-beta blockade in NK therapeutics is independently and sufficiently motivated by TGF-beta's direct suppression of NK activation and cytotoxicity, established without any reference to lineage conversion — Viel S et al., Sci Signal 2016, PMID 26884601 ("TGF-beta inhibits the activation and functions of NK cells by repressing the mTOR pathway"); Laouar Y et al., Nat Immunol 2005, PMID 15852008; Marcoe JP et al., Nat Immunol 2012, PMID 22863752 (all three recovered from the Cortez 2017 reference list). If cNK→trNK conversion is false tomorrow, DNRII NK constructs remain fully justified. A dependency that survives the claim's falsification is not load-bearing on it.

WHAT GENUINELY DEPENDS ON THE CLAIM, and why it is still MEDIUM rather than LOW — CONCRETE NAMED DEPENDENCY: the "intILC1" (CD49a+CD49b+Eomes+) intermediate-state category introduced in Gao et al., Nat Immunol 2017 (PMID 28759001), which is now used as a standing annotation to label CD49a+ clusters in tumour and liver scRNA-seq atlases as an NK-to-ILC1 TRANSITION state. This is a pure inheritance of the claim: the cluster is named for a trajectory rather than a measurement, the naming is then reinforced by pseudotime and RNA velocity (INF_TRAJECTORY, which per G2 cannot establish direction at all), and the annotation feeds back as apparent corroboration. It is load-bearing in the specific sense that if the two-lineage reading is correct, every atlas carrying an "intILC1"/"NK-to-ILC1 transition" label has mis-annotated a distinct resident lineage as a transition state. This is now directly contested by two independent primaries the auditor either missed or under-weighted: Flommersfeld 2021 (PMID 34437840, single-cell barcoding, two separate lineages, no interconversion) and Ducimetière 2021 PNAS (PMID 34183415, cNK and trILC1 as distinct populations with non-redundant roles).

SECOND SURVIVING DEPENDENCY: the clinical-interpretive default that CD49a+ tumour-infiltrating NK cells are "converted/exhausted ex-cNK" rather than a separate resident lineage, which determines whether NKG2A/TGF-beta checkpoint strategies are expected to RESTORE those cells or are aimed at the wrong population entirely.

MEDIUM, not HIGH, because the dependencies are annotational and interpretive rather than therapeutic — no approved or trialled intervention falls if the claim fails. MEDIUM, not LOW, because the mis-annotation is entrenched across the tumour/liver single-cell literature and is self-reinforcing through exactly the trajectory inference G2 forbids.
adv.better_primary_source:
YES — the designated primary source is wrong, though the auditor's own text contains the evidence for why.

PROBLEM WITH CUFF 2016 (PMID 27798170) AS PRIMARY. A.1 asks for the source that FIRST ESTABLISHED THE CLAIM. Cuff 2016's authors explicitly DECLINE to claim conversion — the auditor themselves quote the paper's own inference, "some precursor of the Eomes-hi NK cells could be recruited to the liver from the circulation." A paper whose authors state a precursor-recruitment model cannot be the source that established a mature-cNK-conversion claim. It was selected because it is the earliest date, not because it asserts the claim. Its actual finding — donor Eomes-hi trNK persisting up to 13 years while recipient-origin Eomes-hi NK appear later — is a replenishment-from-outside-the-liver result with an entirely uncontrolled input cell.

BETTER PRIMARY SOURCE FOR THE CLAIM AS WRITTEN: Gao Y et al., "Tumor immunoevasion by the conversion of effector NK cells into type 1 innate lymphoid cells," Nat Immunol 2017;18:1004-1015, PMID 28759001, doi:10.1038/ni.3800. This is the paper that actually asserts the claim, supplies its vocabulary ("conversion", "intILC1"), and is what the downstream literature cites. Designating it is uncomfortable but honest, and it makes the row's real problem visible rather than hiding it: the true primary source for T1 has METHODS THAT CANNOT BE READ (I re-attempted nature.com/articles/ni.3800 and hit the same idp.nature.com paywall — SEARCHED AND UNOBTAINABLE, no PMC deposit, unlike Cortez 2017) AND carries a 2024 Author Correction (PMID 38514890) in which a QIMR Berghofer investigation found Figs 5e, 6d,e and Suppl Figs 5c,d, 8c "believed to have been fabricated or are unreliable." A claim whose originating primary source is simultaneously unreadable and partly unreliable should be graded on that fact.

EARLIEST PRIMARY FOR THE MECHANISTIC SUB-CLAIM (cNK CAN acquire residency markers): Cortez VS et al., Immunity 2016;44:1127-1139, PMID 27156386 — earlier than Cuff 2016 and the first demonstration that WT splenic NK acquire CD49a/CD103/TRAIL/CD73 under TGF-beta1+IL-2. Note its in vivo conclusion is the opposite of T1 (salivary-gland ILCs develop in situ from an early-migrating progenitor), so it is INF_INVITRO support with in vivo refutation attached.

BEST-DESIGNED PRIMARY IN THE WHOLE AREA, IN EITHER DIRECTION: Flommersfeld S et al., Immunity 2021, PMID 34437840, PMC8528403 — the only single-cell clonal fate mapping in mouse. It is counter-evidence, and the auditor's row asserted no such experiment exists.

CORRECTION TO fulltext_available: the auditor recorded Cortez 2017 as having "no PMC deposit." It has one — PMC5712491 / NIHMS921990 — and I retrieved its Methods from the PMC website, which is how the no-adoptive-transfer error surfaced. Their stated reason for the gap was wrong even though a gap remains for Gao 2017.
